Read where a curve and a line meet from a graph, say the coordinates, then zoom in or halve the gap in a table to pin the crossing down." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Two ways to save: one starts ahead, one starts behind. When does the one behind pull level?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8388 url: http://127.0.0.1:8388/index.html readySelector: "#sl-r" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: meet.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Plan A (dashed) starts ahead and adds $300 a year. Plan B (solid) starts lower and grows 20% a year. They meet at about 8.2 years, when both are worth about $4,460." } explainClip: query: { code: "@meet.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "The crossing is where the plans are equal" say: "The crossing is where the two plans are equal." clip: - caption: { text: "The dashed line is the steady plan. The curve grows by a share each year.", say: "The dashed line is the steady plan. The curve grows by a share each year." } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "Where they meet, both are worth the same.", say: "Where they meet, both are worth the same." } - wait: 600 - click: Make r smaller - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "A lower rate pushes the crossing later.", say: "A lower rate pushes the crossing later." } - wait: 1200 --- Two plans for saving. Plan A is steady: $2,000 now, and $300 more each year. Plan B starts with $1,000 and grows by 20% a year. The 20% is made up, and much higher than a real savings account, so that the plans swap places in a short time. ## Predict: who is ahead at 10 years? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to who is ahead after 10 years shows who thinks the plan that starts ahead stays ahead (A) and who sees that a share of a growing balance eventually outgrows the same dollars each year." check: type: predict q: "Plan A starts at $2,000 and adds $300 a year. Plan B starts at $1,000 and grows 20% a year. After 10 years, which plan is worth more, and by about how much?" options: - "Plan B, by about $1{,}200$" - "Plan A, by about $1{,}200$" - "They are equal" - "Plan A, by about $4{,}000$" actual: "Plan B, by about $1,200. Plan A is worth 2,000 + 3,000 = 5,000. Plan B is worth 1,000 × 1.2¹⁰ = 6,192. B started $1,000 behind and ended $1,192 ahead, so the plans swapped places on the way." ``` The bars show where the plans start. Make a guess before you check. ## Run: look for the crossing ```step stage: run insight: "Where the curve meets the line, the two plans are equal. The graph marks that point and gives its coordinates." try: { playground: board, starter: "meet.yml#run", height: 640 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $r$ to 20. Read the point where the plans meet. Between which two whole years is it?", when: "r = 20" } ``` The board marks where the plans meet and gives its coordinates. Change $r$ and watch the crossing move. Which way does it go when $r$ is smaller? ## Investigate: zoom in ```step stage: investigate insight: "The first look gives a window, not an answer. Zooming in narrows the window until the crossing is known to the accuracy you need. Comparing at one time says who is ahead then, not where they swap." try: { playground: board, starter: "meet.yml#zoom1", height: 560 } tasks: - check: type: question q: "In this window the plans meet between which two whole years?" options: ["Between 8 and 9 years", "Between 6 and 7 years", "Between 9 and 10 years", "At exactly 8 years"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "At 6 and 7 years the line is still above the curve.", "By 9 years the curve is already above the line.", "At 8 years the line is 4,400 and the curve is about 4,300: not equal."] explain: "At 8 years the line is ahead (4,400 against 4,300). At 9 years the curve is ahead (5,160 against 4,700). The swap happens between them." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#jo" text: "Jo compares the plans at 10 years. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: one-time-comparison explain: "Line 4: one comparison says who is ahead at that time, not at all times. At 6 years, B is worth about 2,986 and A about 3,800: A is ahead. The plans swap where they cross, at about 8.2 years." - check: type: number q: "Zoom in once more in your head: at 8 years the plans differ by $4,400 - 4,300 = 100$ dollars (A ahead), and at 9 years by $5,160 - 4,700 = 460$ dollars (B ahead). Is the crossing closer to 8 or to 9? Type the closer whole number." answer: 8 explain: "The gap at 8 years is 100 and at 9 years is 460, so the plans are much closer at 8 years. The crossing is just after 8." ``` ### Which window? Read the window before you decide. ```worked 2^x \text{ and } 10 + x :: Where do the curve and the line meet? x = 3:\; 2^3 = 8,\; 10 + 3 = 13 :: The line is ahead. x = 4:\; 2^4 = 16,\; 10 + 4 = 14 :: The curve is ahead. The swap is between 3 and 4. x = 3.5:\; 11.3 \text{ and } 13.5 :: The line is still ahead, so the swap is between 3.5 and 4. x = 3.8:\; 13.9 \text{ and } 13.8 :: The curve is just ahead, so the swap is between 3.5 and 3.8. x \approx 3.8 :: Halve the gap again if you need more places. ``` Now try one on paper: $3^x$ against $20 + x$. At which whole number of $x$ is the curve first ahead? Type it. ### Find the mistake Read Jo's working. Does one comparison show where they swap? ### Closer to which year? ## Modify: change the rate ```step stage: modify insight: "A smaller zoom window gives more figures. A different rate moves the crossing, and a very small rate means the plans may not meet in the window at all." try: { playground: board, starter: "meet.yml#zoom2", height: 560 } tasks: - hint: ["Read the table: the plans swap between two readings.", "8.1 has the line ahead and 8.3 has the curve ahead."] check: { type: answer, q: "In this window ($8$ to $8.4$ years), what is the crossing to 1 decimal place, in years?", answer: "8.2", feedback: [["8", "The window starts at 8, but the plans are not equal yet there: A is worth 4,400 and B about 4,300."], ["8.3", "At 8.3 the curve is already ahead (4,542 against 4,490). The swap is a little earlier."]], explain: "At 8.2 years both are worth about $4,460. The crossing is at about (8.2, 4460)." } - hint: ["Use the value both plans share there.", "Plan A at 8.2 years is $2000 + 300 \\times 8.2$."] check: { type: answer, q: "What is each plan worth at the crossing, in dollars, to the nearest 10 dollars?", answer: "4460", feedback: [["8.2", "8.2 is the time. How much money is each plan worth then?"], ["4400", "That's the line at 8 years. At 8.2 years it is 2,000 + 300 × 8.2."]], explain: "2,000 + 300 × 8.2 = 4,460, and 1,000 × 1.2^8.2 is about 4,460 too." } - hint: "Look at the line: it keeps adding 300 each year. Does the curve ever fall below it again?" check: type: question q: "Edge case: after the crossing, does Plan A ever overtake Plan B again (with 20% a year)?" options: ["No: the curve adds more each year, and the line adds only $300 each year", "Yes: lines are always ahead in the end", "Yes: at about 20 years", "No: curves never come back"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A line adds the same amount each year. The curve adds 20% of a growing balance, which gets bigger.", "After the crossing the gap grows: at 10 years it is about 1,192 in B's favour.", "Curves can swing back; here it doesn't happen because the curve adds more each year."] explain: "After 8.2 years Plan B adds more each year than $300, so the gap only grows." ``` ### Reading the window ### The value there ### Does it swap back? ## Practise: find the crossing ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading a crossing from two values, from a bracket of years, and (review) finding where two lines meet." tasks: - check: type: question q: "At 5 years Plan A is worth $4,000$ and Plan B is worth $3,200$. At 6 years A is worth $4,300$ and B is worth $4,000$. At 7 years A is worth $4,600$ and B is worth $5,000$. Between which two years do they meet?" options: ["Between 6 and 7 years", "Between 5 and 6 years", "At 6 years", "After 7 years"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "At 6 years A is still ahead (4,300 against 4,000).", "At 6 years the plans are 300 apart.", "At 7 years B is already ahead."] explain: "A is ahead at 6 years and B is ahead at 7 years, so they swap between 6 and 7." smaller: check: { type: question, q: "At 6 years A is worth $4,300$ and B is worth $4,000$. Which is ahead?", options: ["A", "B", "Neither"], answer: 0, explain: "4,300 is more than 4,000, so A is ahead." } - check: type: number q: "A table shows $2^x$ and $x + 12$. At $x = 3$ they are $8$ and $15$. At $x = 4$ they are $16$ and $16$. At what $x$ do they meet?" answer: 4 explain: "At x = 4 both are 16." - check: type: question q: "At 2 years $2^x$ is 4 and $3x$ is 6. At 3 years they are 8 and 9. At 4 years they are 16 and 12. Which statement is right?" options: ["The curve overtakes the line between 3 and 4 years", "The curve overtakes the line between 2 and 3 years", "The curve is always below the line", "They meet at exactly 3 years"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "At 3 years the line is still ahead (9 against 8).", "At 4 years the curve is ahead (16 against 12).", "At 3 years they are 8 and 9, not equal."] explain: "The line is ahead at 3 years and the curve is ahead at 4 years, so the swap is between." - check: type: number q: "Review: two lines $y = 2x + 1$ and $y = x + 5$ meet where $2x + 1 = x + 5$. What is $x$?" answer: 4 explain: "2x + 1 = x + 5, so x = 4." ``` ### Between which years? ### Which is ahead? ### A curve overtakes ### Review From the last unit: where two lines meet. ## Make: back to the plans ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the savings: the crossing is the decision. Before it the steady plan wins, after it the compounding one wins, so the right choice depends on how long you save." try: { playground: board, starter: "meet.yml#vary", height: 640 } tasks: - hint: ["Plan A at 6 years is 2,000 + 300 × 6.", "Plan B at 6 years is 1,000 × 1.2⁶."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "At 6 years, how many dollars is Plan A worth more than Plan B? Use $r = 20$. Round to the nearest dollar." steps: - ["$2000 + 300 \\times 6 = 3800$", "plan A at 6 years"] - ["$1000 \\times 1.2^6 = 2986$", "plan B at 6 years"] - ["$3800 - 2986 = 814$", "how much more A is worth"] answer: "814" answerLabel: "Dollars more" tolerance: 0.5 feedback: - ["2986", "That's plan B. Subtract it from plan A."] - ["3800", "That's plan A. Find how much more it is than plan B."] criteria: - "I worked out both plans at 6 years." - "I used 1.2, not 0.2, as the factor." - "I subtracted in the right order and gave dollars." explain: "3,800 − 2,986 = 814, so A is ahead by about $814 at 6 years." - check: type: question q: "A friend plans to save for 5 years only. Using these plans with 20% a year, which should they pick?" options: ["Plan A: the plans don't meet until about 8.2 years, and A is ahead until then", "Plan B: it grows faster", "Either: they are equal at 5 years", "Plan B: curves always win"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "B grows faster in the end, but at 5 years A is worth 3,500 and B is worth about 2,488.", "They are equal only at the crossing, about 8.2 years.", "A curve wins only after the crossing."] explain: "Before about 8.2 years A is worth more. A saver for 5 years should pick A, and one for 10 should pick B." ``` ### How far ahead? Back to the plans. Work it out on paper first, then type your answer. ### Which plan for 5 years? The decision is the crossing. The 20% a year is made up and much higher than a real savings account, so that the crossing is within a few years. Sources: the two plans and the 20% a year are made up for this lesson. **Also used in** - **Phone plans.** A plan with a low fee and a high price per gigabyte meets a plan with a high fee and a low price per gigabyte, and the crossing says which to pick. - **Science.** Where a measured line meets a predicted curve is where the model agrees with the data. - **Next lesson.** Circles: relations that are not functions. ```teacher summary: Students find where an exponential curve and a line meet from a graph, state the coordinates, and refine the answer by zooming in or by halving the gap in a table (AC9M10A05, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can read where two graphs meet and say what the coordinates mean. - I can narrow a crossing down by zooming in or by comparing values in a table. - I can say which plan is better before and after the crossing. struggle: Stopping at one comparison. Ask 'is that true for every year, or just that one?' and have them check a second year on the other side. before: > Do the three boards yourself first: the full window (Run), the 6 to 10 window (Investigate) and the 8 to 8.4 window (Modify). Students need the exponential model from lesson 6 and where two lines meet from Year 9. The one idea: the crossing is the decision. Before it one plan wins and after it the other, so the right choice depends on how long you save. The first graph gives a window, not an answer; zooming in or halving the gap narrows it to the accuracy you need. All numbers are made up: $2,000 and $300 a year for plan A, $1,000 and 20% a year for plan B. 20% is much higher than a real savings account; it is chosen so the plans swap in a short time. Say so in class. The board marks the crossing with its coordinates (8.2, 4460). The board has no zoom control, so the zoom is three boards with smaller windows. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose Plan A assumed the plan that starts ahead stays ahead. Don't correct it yet." - "Run: ask students to move r and say which way the crossing goes." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the dollars gap in Make are worked on paper first. Look for the two values written side by side at each x." - "Modify: before the 'swap back' edge case, ask what the line adds each year and what the curve adds." stuck: - see: A student compares at one time only (Jo's mistake). ask: Is the same plan ahead at 6 years? fix: Check one year on each side. If the leader changes, the plans cross in between. - see: A student reads the crossing as a point on one axis only (8.2, or 4460). ask: What are the two numbers, and what does each one mean? fix: "Write it as a point: 8.2 years is the time, $4,460 is the amount both plans are worth then." - see: A student stops at 'between 8 and 9' when asked for 1 decimal place. ask: Which of 8.1, 8.2 and 8.3 is closest to equal? fix: Make a table at those values and compare the two columns. stretch: "Find a rate r for which the plans meet at about 5 years. Then: is there a rate for which they never meet in 15 years? Which of the three windows is the board using when you do?" support: Print the table for 6 to 10 years and highlight which plan is larger in each row. Draw a line where the highlight changes. leads: > Next: circles as relations. They have a centre and a radius, and they are not functions. Where it leads in class: choosing between plans, break-even points and when one model overtakes another. exit: q: Plan A is worth 1,000 + 200x and Plan B is worth 500 × 1.5ˣ. At x = 3 A is 1,600 and B is 1,687.5. At x = 2 A is 1,400 and B is 1,125. Between which two values of x do they meet? a: "Between 2 and 3: A is ahead at 2 and B is ahead at 3." explain: > Where two graphs meet, the two values are **equal**. The coordinates of that point tell you both the time and the common value. To find a crossing exactly enough: 1. Read a window from the graph. 2. Zoom in on that window, or make a table of the two values in it. 3. Find where the one in front changes, and halve the gap again if you need more figures. sources: - title: "Made up for this lesson: Plan A ($2,000 and $300 a year) and Plan B ($1,000 and 20% a year) are not real accounts." url: https://tutorials.learningwaypoints.com/maths/functions/where-they-meet/ checked: 2026-10-25 ```

# Boards for "Where they meet". x is the number of years. Plan A saves $2,000 now and adds $300 a year (steady).
# Plan B starts with $1,000 and grows by r% a year (r is made up). Where the curve meets the line, the plans are equal.
# zoom1 and zoom2 show the same plans with a smaller window around the crossing at r = 20: (8.2, 4460).

# region: run
widget: graph
x: 0, 15
y: 0, 8000
grid: 5, 2000
axes: Time (years), Savings ($)
slider r: 5, 30, 10, 5
plot: y = 1000((1 + r/100)^x)
plot: y = 2000 + 300x, dashed
cross: 1, 2
table: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: graph
x: 0, 15
y: 0, 8000
grid: 5, 2000
axes: Time (years), Savings ($)

plot: y = 1000((1 + r/100)^x)

cross: 1, 2
table: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
# endregion

# Jo's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: jo
Plan A is 2000 + 300x. Plan B is 1000(1.2^x). Which is the better plan?
At 10 years, A = 2000 + 3000 = 5000 and B = 1000 x 1.2^10 = 6192.
B is bigger at 10 years, so B is the better plan.
B is the better plan, whatever the number of years.
# endregion
